name: deliverable
shape: A client deliverable. A readout deck built for one engagement, not for publication.
template: Set by the engagement, not by this profile.
measuredFrom: The ExampleSlides corpus's ten client decks, 682 working pages. Re-baselined 2026-08-29; before that the constants came from a single 167-page reference market study (190 median words per page, 19-word titles, 74% carrying a number, floor 0.65), carried inline in audit.mjs and density.mjs before profiles existed.
notes: Re-baselined 2026-08-29, by decision. The one-deck reference numbers were kept when this file first appeared so the calibration and the profile mechanism could not move in one change; once the mechanism had held stable across sessions, the ten-deck corpus replaced them. Measured before moved: all four live decks read identically under both calibrations (Argo and commercial-diligence clear the number floor at 77% and 80% under either; firm-overview and robotics-components sit at 0% and fail under either), so this changed what the baselines claim, not what any gate says. The floor keeps its old distance of nine points under the share, which also matches the report profile's floor exactly. Note the house style runs hotter than the corpus (217 to 249 words per page, 77 to 80% numbered on the analytic decks); the widened printed gap is information, not a fault.
pages is null: this profile sets no page budget. The reference deliverable runs 167 pages and Project Argo runs 81, so any budget wide enough for both would not be a check.

thinShare is 0. On a client page, under 120 words usually is a placeholder that has been styled. On a published research page it is a form, which is why the research profiles expect two fifths of their pages to be thin.
